function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves the data from the response. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media Types that are acceptable for the response.

Authorization.description: Authorization credentials for connecting to a resource.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request.

timeout.description: The maximum number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float value. This is a float type value.

limit.description: The maximum number of results to return.

params.description: A dictionary of URL parameters to append to the URL.

auth.description: A tuple representing the auth (username, password) to enable HTTP authentication. Use None for no authentication.

cert.description: A string specifying a cert file path, or a tuple specifying cert and key file paths for SSL client authentication. Use None for no certificate.

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP connections.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS connections.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol or protocol and hostname to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will be immediately downloaded; otherwise, the response will be streamed.

verify.description: A boolean that controls whether to verify the server's TLS certificate, or a string that must be a path to a CA bundle to use. Defaults to True.
